newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP eyes scrapping land tax in 98/99 -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP eyes scrapping land tax in 98/99 -- paper.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) is set to discuss freezing or scrapping a tax on land holdings when it sets overall tax policies for the year starting in April 1998, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

Yoshiro Hayashi, chairman of the LDP's tax research council, was quoted by the mass circulation daily Mainichi Shimbun as saying in an interview that the LDP and other parties will likely discuss whether to axe or freeze the land-holding tax at that time.

The land-holding tax was designed to dent the 1980s economic bubble of inflated asset prices, Hayashi was quoted as saying. "It's necessary to prevent reemergence of land speculation such as we saw during the bubble era. But given the current land price situation, I believe we can rely on the tax on fixed assets alone as a way to levy taxes on land holdings."

The rate of the land-holding tax now stands at 1.5 percent. Some legislators and business leaders have urged the government to suspend or freeze the tax, introduced in 1992, saying it has already fulfilled its initial purpose of curbing speculative land trade rampant during the bubble era.

Hayashi was also quoted by the paper as saying he was aware of calls for the abolition of a securities transaction tax, but that Japan must first decide whether it wanted to rely on the capital gains tax alone if it scrapped the securities transaction tax.
